pages.title: AI assistance and autonomous workflows
pages.description: Configure an assistant and give an autonomous workflow a precise, testable objective.
pages.html:
Open AI assistant settings to configure a supported signed-in CLI or HTTP provider, model and limits. A CLI connection uses its existing account; an HTTP provider may require its own key and billing. Keys belong in the application's credential mechanism, never source files, scenario JSON, screenshots or job parameters. Local providers still need their own running service/model.

Choose an interaction mode#

Mode Use
Autonomous workflow Investigate, reconstruct, patch or port/test through tool operations
Conversation Ask about a program; review tool use and the answer
Function Explain, suggest names or convert the selected function

The Workspace side panel and dedicated AI page expose these modes. Select a project/function before a focused action. Conversion produces editable source with a separate compiler-check state; it does not by itself patch the executable.

  1. Define the task — Specify scope and expected behavior.
  2. Inspect evidence — Discover tools and prerequisites.
  3. Plan bounded work — Keep steps and retries finite.
  4. Back up and edit — Check source revisions and history.
  5. Build and verify — Require actual recorded results.
  6. Report or resume — Retain checkpoints and unknowns.

Give a testable task#

Describe the target, intended change, permitted source scope, required output and a concrete acceptance scenario. For example: explain a selected export routine, reconstruct its project, change the output format, build it and compare a specified input/output case. Configure bounded tool steps, repair attempts and token limits rather than asking for unlimited retries.

The agent discovers Runtime operations, records checkpoints, creates source-history backups and inspects errors. Saved source buffers are protected while it changes the project. Progress and resumable status are available through the agent status operation. Provider failures, cancellation, missing tools and stale source revisions can interrupt the run; inspect the last checkpoint before resuming.

Verify the result#

Read changes, compilation output, source commits, modified-copy receipts and recorded scenarios. Completion of a workflow requires its validation evidence, not just a confident response. A successful model request is distinct from a successful build, test or equivalent application. No AI provider can recover missing encrypted bytes or guarantee every game/application will rebuild.

For external clients, see MCP / CLI. For automatic repair behavior, see reconstruction; for function changes, see replacement.

pages.title: AI assistance
pages.description: Public operations for this workflow.
pages.html:
Start with the user guide.

  • ai_status — Configured AI provider/model, availability of every provider and compile checkers.
  • ai_configure — Choose the AI provider and model and the assistant limits. API keys are not accepted here; store them in the window (Options > AI) or in the provider environment variable.
  • ai_explain — Explain a function/unit in Markdown: summary, step by step, inputs/outputs, notable details.
  • ai_rename — Propose names for the function and its variables (and a one-line comment); apply=true stores them as renames.
  • ai_convert — Turn pseudo-code, disassembly or bytecode into clean compilable source in a target language, then compile-check it and let the AI repair errors.
  • ai_agent — Autonomously investigate, reconstruct, patch or port the selected project using live operation schemas and authenticated child jobs. Recovers from tool/build errors, installs missing official components when enabled, saves checkpoints and requires recorded validation before completion. Existing AI provider credentials are required.
  • ai_agent_status — Read persisted autonomous task progress and evidence, including after cancellation or a restart.
  • ai_ask — Ask a question about the program. The assistant navigates the analysis with tools (list, decompile, xrefs, strings, search) and answers; conversations can be continued.
  • ai_batch_rename — Name many auto-named functions (FUN_*, sub_*) in one job and apply the names.
  • ai_conversations — Conversations stored for a project.
  • ai_conversation — Turns of one conversation.

pages.title: Inspect and export code
pages.description: Public operations for this workflow.
pages.html:
Start with the user guide.

  • open_file — Open a binary, assembly, archive, bytecode or shader file as a project (deduplicated by SHA256), detect its format and, by default, analyze it with the best installed engine.
  • analyze — Analyze a project with an engine (Ghidra, native, ILSpy, Vineflower, JADX, Python, shader).
  • list_projects — Every project with its analyses.
  • project_info — Format, architecture, sections, imports, exports, counts, shader reflection and notes.
  • delete_project — Delete a project and its analyses, caches and AI results. The original file is untouched.
  • list_functions — Functions, types or code units of an analysis, filtered and paginated.
  • function_info — One unit: signature, callers, callees, imports, strings, comment and local renames.
  • decompile — Decompiled source (or disassembly) of one unit, with the user's renames and comments applied.
  • xrefs — Callers, callees and imports of a unit.
  • strings — Strings found by the analysis, filtered and paginated.
  • search — Search function names, cached decompiled code and strings.
  • rename — Rename a function/global (or, with function, a local identifier). Applied to every view.
  • set_comment — Attach a comment to a unit (empty text removes it).
  • set_notes — Free-form notes for the whole project.
  • export_sources — Write every unit's code (annotations applied) as files: into the job workspace, or into destination when given. .NET can also produce a compilable C# project.
  • c_module — x86 / x86-64 / ARM64: decompile functions (and, by default, everything they call) with the built-in C decompiler into ONE C file meant to compile again (MSVC / clang): globals are initialised from the image, constants inlined, prototypes emitted. Empty functions = every exported function.
  • extract_embedded — Extract what an executable carries: PyInstaller bundles (entry scripts and modules as .pyc), .NET single-file bundles (assemblies), UPX-packed files (unpacked original) and appended zip archives. Each extracted file can then be opened with open_file.
  • extracted_files — List the files of a previous extraction.
  • load_symbols — Find the PDB of a PE file (local folders, next to the original file, then the symbol server) and read its function names. Re-analyze afterwards to apply them.

pages.title: Console workflows
pages.description: Public operations for this workflow.
pages.html:
Start with the user guide.

  • unreal_rules — Read bundled reconstruction rules, validation requirements and campaign profiles from the Halo CEA Unreal prototype. Read-only knowledge integration; does not import assets, build or convert a game.
  • unreal_guide — Render the same bundled rules as a portable Markdown guide, with source snapshot hashes and explicit limits. No game execution.
  • xbox_open — Prepare a preserved Xbox XBE/Xbox 360 XEX, extracted game folder, XDVDFS ISO or ZIP containing one ISO. Folder/disc resources are copied into a persistent game project. No emulator or game is started.
  • xbox_info — Read preserved console metadata, exact executable identity, prepared assets and native build state.
  • xbox_tools — Inspect or configure the separate ReXGlue SDK and optional locally built native GPU plugin.
  • xbox_install — Install the official pinned ReXGlue 0.10.0 Windows SDK separately under runtime/engines, with SHA-256 verification.
  • xbox_attach — Register a local ReXGlue native project after checking its manifest, original XEX and existing build receipt. No compilation, game execution or asset copy occurs.
  • xbox_create — Generate an editable CMake/ReXGlue project from prepared input. Exact-SHA Halo profiles are applied only to their matching executable. Original Xbox XBE native recompilation is not implemented.
  • xbox_build — Generate CPU C++ and build the selected native project through cancellable owned subprocesses. Compilation/link success does not establish gameplay compatibility.
  • xbox_run — Verify original executable, compiled executable and recorded GPU plugin hashes, then run the native PC game. The Runtime owns the process tree; cancellation stops the game. No Xbox Live or emulator process.
  • xbox_guide — Read the shipped method, exact-image patching rules, renderer/input/timing pitfalls and current compatibility limits.
  • porting_open — Persistently import one local file or folder. Built-in ZIP and plaintext SELF preparation; PKG/PFS/RAR/7z use a configured separate UltraPack backend. Originals are preserved. No decryption.
  • porting_info — Read the saved input manifest, ELF evidence and preparation limits.
  • porting_tools — Read or configure separate converter, target-library and UltraPack CLI paths. Does not execute tools.
  • porting_install — Install separate official AnyPS5 converter and target libraries with published SHA-256 digests, or UltraPack source at a resolved Git commit with a private Python environment and optional .NET package helper.
  • porting_plan — Check prepared input and selected tools. This is not a claim of game compatibility.
  • porting_convert — Convert a verified application snapshot using the separately configured AnyPS5 converter. Write a separate receipt-verified output with libraries and resources; behavior remains unverified.
  • porting_conversion — Read the saved conversion receipt and output manifest.
  • porting_run — Verify receipt hashes, copy the output into a job-owned directory, then run bounded scenarios on the matching host. No assertions means executed-unverified, not behavioral validation.
  • porting_diagnose — Analyze verified guest ELF bytes with cdec, native or Ghidra. Link saved AnyPS5 registry file offsets and conversion errors to decoded instructions/functions; include assembly/C samples and runtime trace candidates without guessing host-to-guest address mappings. Does not patch or execute the application.

pages.title: Investigate and compare behavior
pages.description: Public operations for this workflow.
pages.html:
Start with the user guide.

  • application_open — Capture a bounded immutable folder, ASAR or JS/TS/HTML artifact snapshot and analyze it with the inert TypeScript AST parser. Excluded artifacts are reported.
  • investigation_native — Read-only Ghidra function dossier: type layouts, instruction references, call sites and bounded high p-code SSA value dependencies. Requires existing Ghidra analysis.
  • investigation_query — Find feature text, names or endpoints and return related graph nodes with explicit relationship paths, hash-bound source locations, observations, inferences and unknowns.
  • investigation_source — Read a source from the immutable application snapshot and verify its SHA256.
  • investigation_har — Import HAR metadata and correlate exact literal URLs or paths with route/endpoint candidates. Request headers, cookies and bodies are not retained; no URL is fetched.
  • behavior_capture — Run an explicitly selected executable in a fresh working directory. Record text streams, exit status, file changes, optional owned TCP connections and Windows/Chromium/Electron graphical scenarios. This is not an OS sandbox; external file writes and traffic outside the observation scope are not captured.
  • behavior_captures — Recordings retained for this project.
  • behavior_evidence — Read retained GUI steps, DOM/UI Automation states, HTTP/TCP observations and hash-verified screenshot paths.
  • behavior_compare — Compare recorded text outputs, termination, file hashes, HTTP/TCP observations, GUI states and screenshots for the same replay scenario. Matching observations do not establish program equivalence.

pages.title: Replace functions and debug
pages.description: Public operations for this workflow.
pages.html:
Start with the user guide.

  • debug_status — Snapshot of the in-memory .NET debug session, current pause and console.
  • debug_breakpoints — Read or replace persistent C# source breakpoints while no debug session is active.
  • debug_start — Build the startup C# project in Debug with portable PDB, or launch a verified modified-copy receipt with regenerated symbols, then launch NetCoreDbg. This job owns the session until it ends: cancel it to kill the adapter and application tree. Use separate debug_status/debug_control jobs while it runs. NetCoreDbg must be installed explicitly.
  • debug_control — Continue, pause, step, stop, inspect threads/frames/locals or expand a variable. Paused commands require the current stopId to reject stale frame/variable handles. No arbitrary DAP requests, expression evaluation or attach to an existing process.
  • patch_prepare — Compile a native x86/x64 PE replacement. Default mode verifies a leaf function in place; extended mode appends linked code/data, resolves existing functions/imports, merges x64 unwind tables and ASLR relocations, and redirects the original entry. Preserve the original signature/ABI.
  • patch_apply — Revalidate a prepared patch and write a separate EXE/DLL copy with checksum and receipt. Never overwrite the original or an existing output. Authenticode signatures are invalidated.
  • patch_outputs — List persistent verified patch receipts and the last completed copy run.
  • patch_run — Execute a saved modified application copy after revalidating its hash and copied dependencies. Never run the original or load a DLL into the Tool. Stream stdout/stderr, kill the process tree on cancellation or timeout.
  • managed_methods — Read metadata tokens and exact method signatures without executing the assembly. Build the private dnlib helper from pinned, hash-locked NuGet dependencies when needed.
  • managed_patch_prepare — Build the edited C# project and replace a selected source method in a verified preview of the original assembly. Import isolated compiler-generated closures/local functions and async/iterator state machines. Remap IL and verify all existing other method bodies/tokens unchanged. Optionally import compatible new user-defined dependencies and emit remapped portable PDBs. Reject signature/layout/initializer changes, R2R and mixed mode.

pages.title: Edit and reconstruct projects
pages.description: Public operations for this workflow.
pages.html:
Start with the user guide.

  • workspace_history — Keep exact source/resource/dependency snapshots in a private local Git repository per attached folder. Status lists versions; snapshot saves a described version; compare previews changes against a commit. Restore requires its preview revision, saves current files first and creates a restoration commit. Build output and VCS folders are excluded. No remotes, user index or hooks are used.
  • workspace_refactor_check — Reject a stale source snapshot before applying a refactoring to editor buffers.
  • workspace_evaluate — Explicitly execute ResolveReferences and read evaluated Compile/ReferencePath/ProjectReference metadata. Custom MSBuild targets may run. Cache the model for editor requests until project configuration changes.
  • workspace_info — Source workspace, editable files and last build.
  • workspace_create — Reconstruct an editable .NET solution, native executable/shared/static project, or Node/web/Electron source workspace. Report missing entry points, dependencies, exports and initialization rather than inventing recovered behavior.
  • workspace_open — Attach an existing C#, VC++, CMake or multi-project solution folder to an analysis project.
  • workspace_read — Read a confined UTF-8 source file and its revision.
  • workspace_save — Save edited source atomically, refusing concurrent disk changes.
  • workspace_search — Search saved UTF-8 source files by literal text and return clickable file/line/column matches. Exclude build output and binary files; bound results and scan size.
  • workspace_csharp — Use installed SDK Roslyn for completion, definitions, references, diagnostics and reviewed semantic rename/format edits across source projects and unsaved buffers. Read project/reference metadata without executing user MSBuild targets or analyzers. Custom build targets/generators require a normal build for complete diagnostics.
  • workspace_execute — Run cancellable .NET SDK, MSBuild, CMake/CTest or JavaScript/TypeScript/npm jobs; return output and file/line diagnostics. Run and test execute code. A native library needs an executable/test harness.
  • workspace_dependencies — Explicit npm ci from the recovered lockfile, with lifecycle scripts disabled. Native modules may still require ABI rebuilds.
  • reconstruction_status — Read the last durable reconstruction report, build rounds, Git commits and scenario evidence.
  • reconstruction_run — Create a workspace if necessary and perform up to ten build rounds. Optional AI source corrections use the configured provider, revision guards and private Git history. Compare original/rebuilt outputs, files, network and graphics with recorded scenarios. scenarios-matched applies only to observed scenarios; compiled-unverified is not equivalence.

pages.title: Engines, settings and updates
pages.description: Public operations for this workflow.
pages.html:
Start with the user guide.

  • symbols_configure — PDB lookup: enable/disable, symbol server (HTTPS; empty = local folders only) and local folders.
  • list_engines — Engines with formats, licence and availability.
  • list_components — Downloadable components (JDK, Ghidra, .NET, ILSpy, Vineflower, JADX, Python decompilers) with installed versions, system installs and overrides.
  • install_component — Download the current release of a component from its official source, verify it (SHA256/SHA512 when published) and install it under runtime/engines.
  • remove_component — Remove a privately installed component version (system installs are never touched).
  • set_component_path — Use a component already installed elsewhere (e.g. a Ghidra folder or a JDK). Empty clears it.
  • update_state — Installed version, configured repository, staged update and kept versions.
  • update_configure — Set the GitHub repository (owner/name) that publishes CyDecompilator releases, and automatic checks.
  • update_check — Ask GitHub for the latest application release.
  • update_download — Download a release into runtime/updates and verify it (identity, runtime ABI, digest, compilation).
  • update_apply — Activate the staged update (keeps the current app/ in runtime/backups; data/ is untouched). Restart afterwards.
  • update_rollback — Restore the app/ kept by the last update.

Restart afterwards. update_rollback — Restore the app/ kept by the last update.

pages.title: MCP, CLI and operation reference
pages.description: Connect an MCP client or CLI and follow the operation/job protocol.
pages.html:
The GUI, CLI and MCP expose the same Runtime business operations. Open Advanced operations to browse the installed operation contracts, parameter forms, declared permissions and outputs. This live catalogue is the reference for the exact installed version; do not rely on a fixed operation count in a guide or an AI prompt.

Connect an MCP client#

Use the installation's private Python and app/tool.py mcp as a stdio server. Replace these example installation paths with your actual location:

json
{  "mcpServers": {    "cydecompilator": {      "command": "C:/Tools/CyDecompilator/runtime/python/Scripts/python.exe",      "args": ["C:/Tools/CyDecompilator/app/tool.py", "mcp"]    }  }}

If the desktop/another server already owns the job database, use a distinct absolute job directory with --data-dir, placed before mcp in the arguments. Analysis projects are still shared by the installation: coordinate mutations to the same project across clients. Install the bundled CyDecompilator skill using app/scripts/install_skill.py when your client supports skills; installing it does not configure MCP automatically.

Discover, submit, wait, inspect#

Use cy_describe_operation before constructing parameters. Business tools are named op_... and use a parameters envelope. Control tools such as cy_get_job take their own arguments directly:

json
{"tool":"op_open_file","arguments":{"parameters":{"path":"C:/samples/App.dll","engine":"ilspy"}}}

The returned job identifier is not the result. Poll cy_get_job until Completed, Failed or Cancelled, then read outputs/error. A completed job can still contain a build/test result whose status is failed or unverified. Preserve project, plan, receipt and capture IDs between dependent operations. Do not invent IDs or treat model prose as execution evidence.

CLI and permissions#

The private interpreter can run app/tool.py list-operations and invoke with a parameters file and an explicit timeout. The installed contract determines which operations need network, process spawning or external filesystem permissions. A restricted client must have those permissions explicitly; never put a token in business parameters. Reading this manual or following its local links grants no execution permissions and runs no commands.

See AI, projects and observations for the corresponding workflows.

pages.title: Console inputs and native projects
pages.description: Choose a console workflow and understand its prerequisites and limits.
pages.html:
Start with complete, readable files that you can analyze. Keep the original separate from generated projects and converted executables.

Choose a workflow#

Input or objective Open What it does
PS5 ELF, plaintext SELF, extracted application or supported container PS5 porting Prepare input, configure AnyPS5/UltraPack, convert and run explicit scenarios
Xbox XBE, Xbox 360 XEX, extracted game or XDVDFS image Xbox porting Prepare input; generate, compile or attach supported Xbox 360 native projects
Rebuild an understood subsystem in Unreal Unreal reconstruction Consult rules and profiles, then implement and compare a specific feature

These workflows do not supply a universal console-to-PC or console-to-Unreal port. Original Xbox native recompilation and general PS3/PS4 conversion are not available through these controls. A native analysis engine can inspect a readable executable without making its operating-system or graphics interfaces compatible with the PC.

Keep work manageable#

Check free space before importing a whole game. A preserved input, converted output, native source tree and compiler cache occupy separate storage. Use an existing native project attachment when you already have a suitable build; do not repeat an import just to reopen it. See storage and the Xbox methods.

pages.title: Debug reconstructed .NET sources
pages.description: Start a .NET debug session, manage breakpoints and inspect paused variables.
pages.html:
The integrated debugger uses NetCoreDbg for supported .NET projects and modified managed copies. It is not a general native/Java/Python debugger. Debugging requires a runnable compatible output, matching source files and usable symbols, usually portable PDBs.

Start a session#

  1. Install/configure the debugger from its offered component control.
  2. Open the source project, save changes, build the desired configuration and select its startup target.
  3. Open the relevant source file and place a breakpoint. Unsaved files must be saved first.
  4. Start debugging the project, or use Debug modified copy for a verified saved managed patch.
  5. Read Debugger status. A requested breakpoint may remain unverified until matching symbols are loaded.

Pause and inspect#

When paused, use Stack and variables to select a thread/frame and inspect available locals. Add watches and evaluate supported expressions in the selected context. Continue/Pause, Step over, Step into and Step out control execution. F5 continues a paused active session; F9 toggles a breakpoint in the focused source editor. Use the visible controls when focus is elsewhere.

Debugger values and pause handles belong to the active session. Do not reuse them after continuing, restarting or stopping. A failed watch can mean an unavailable variable, invalid expression, optimized code or a stale frame rather than a target crash.

Keep source correspondence#

Source files become read-only during debugging. If they change externally, stop, rebuild and restart before trusting line correspondence. The debugger is a job-owned process: Stop debugging ends the session, and cancellation handles its process tree. An exit code is recorded separately from breakpoint/inspection success.

Diagnose common failures#

Symptom Check
No runnable target Startup project, executable output and matching .NET runtime
Breakpoint not bound PDB identity, source revision and optimization
Wrong source location Rebuild after changes; confirm the selected module
Variables unavailable Selected frame, scope, optimized code and pause state
Copy no longer accepted Patch receipt integrity and fresh build/plan

See projects, method replacement and troubleshooting.

pages.title: Engines and supported inputs
pages.description: Select an engine for the detected format and install its optional components.
pages.html:
Open Engines to inspect component status, install an optional engine or configure an existing compatible executable. Downloads use official sources and available integrity metadata; engines stay separate from the application's private Python. Engine installation may require a network connection even though this manual does not.

Pick an engine#

Input Engine Expected view
Native PE/ELF, x86/x64/ARM64 CyDecompilator C Structured C where supported
Native binaries and firmware Ghidra, when installed C pseudocode and richer native analysis
Native machine code Built-in disassembler Instructions, calls, imports and strings
Managed .NET assemblies ILSpy C# and source-project export
Java classes/JAR Vineflower Java sources
Android APK/DEX JADX Java and Android resources/manifest
Python bytecode Python engine Supported recovered source or bytecode view
DXBC, DXIL, SPIR-V shaders Built-in shader engine HLSL/GLSL and bytecode/instructions
JS/TS/HTML/ASAR application Investigation parser Modules, source-map and feature evidence

The program detects input contents, not just the filename extension. A renamed executable does not become another format. Available engines appear in the Workspace selector. Selecting an engine without cached results starts its analysis; Re-analyze refreshes results for that engine. A different engine may recover different functions, names or pseudocode without either output being original source.

Install or select an existing tool#

  1. Find the component, inspect its status and prerequisites, then choose Install when necessary.
  2. For an existing Java, .NET, Ghidra or other supported tool, use its path-selection control and validate the selected executable/version.
  3. Return to Workspace and start analysis. Check the task output for missing dependencies, unsupported architecture or timeouts.

Ghidra/Java, managed services, TypeScript/Node.js and console-conversion tools have separate prerequisites. Installing one does not install all the others. Compiler/debugger availability is also separate from decompiler availability.

Format-specific limits#

See native analysis for inferred types and unsupported instructions; .NET, Java, Python and shaders for source recovery limits. Packed applications may first need extraction. Encryption, unavailable original dependencies, protected code and dynamically generated code can prevent analysis. Increase bounded analysis limits only when the report identifies a limit; a longer timeout cannot recover unavailable bytes.

pages.title: Native help-link API
pages.description: Open a validated local chapter, section or annotated image from Python.
pages.html:
The application uses the Python documentation module to resolve local help links. It reads the packaged route catalogue, accepts supported legacy chapter names and refuses unknown destinations. Import it from an installed application's module path.

Open a chapter#

python
from documentation import Documentation help = Documentation()help.open('projects', 'fr', anchor='edit-and-build')

Documentation(root=None, opener=None) uses the Documentation directory beside documentation.py by default. An explicit root selects another complete installed export. The optional opener has the webbrowser.open(url, new=0) contract; returning false reports a browser-launch error.

Public methods#

  • Documentation.url returns an encoded local URL without opening it.
  • Documentation.open validates the same destination and opens it.

Both methods accept the same page, language, section and media-view fields. English is the default. French variants such as fr-CA select French; other interface languages select English. Stable page and annotation identifiers are common to both editions.

An annotated image#

python
url = help.url('start', 'en', media='workspace-screenshot',               note='function-list', zoom=1.25)

The image is already distributed with the manual. A link does not import a new media file or execute inspected application code. Browser policies can affect persistent reading preferences for local files.

pages.title: Local help links
pages.description: Create and open validated local links to help chapters.
pages.html:
Build a validated file URL for the installed CyDoc export. The default language is English; French is retained and other interface languages fall back to English. Legacy chapter filenames and translated heading slugs resolve through the packaged compatibility map. Unknown pages, anchors, media and media state are rejected.

python
from documentation import Documentationhelp = Documentation()url = help.url('start', 'fr', media='workspace-screenshot', note='function-list')

Signature#

text
Documentation.url(topic='start', language='en', anchor='', media='', **state) -> str

Parameters#

topic is a stable chapter ID or supported legacy alias. language selects English or French. anchor names an explicit section. media names a distributed image; optional note, zoom, x and y select its annotation and view. A zoom must be finite and between 0.25 and 12.

Returns and errors#

Returns an encoded absolute file:// URL to Documentation/Documentation.html. This method does not open a browser. Unknown destinations or invalid view values raise ValueError; a missing reader raises FileNotFoundError.

See the user guide and the integration API.

pages.title: Git history and source comparisons
pages.description: Save source versions, preview changes and restore through private local Git history.
pages.html:
Project IDE → Git history stores private local source versions. Git must be installed and available on PATH. This history is separate from any existing Git repository in the attached source folder and separate from CyDecompilator's own development repository.

Save and compare#

  1. Save open files so the disk state matches the intended source version.
  2. Enter a meaningful description and choose Save Git version.
  3. Edit the source or resources, then select a saved version.
  4. Choose Compare with saved sources, then select a changed file. The shared diff view provides side-by-side changes, next-change navigation and text search. Raw text is available for copying.

Restore deliberately#

Review the comparison and save pending editor buffers before choosing Restore this version. Restoration first saves the current state in a recoverable commit, then records the restored state as another commit. Open files are reloaded. Source-revision checks refuse a restore whose preview no longer matches the files. A restore is not a silent reset of the source folder's own repository.

What is included#

Sources, resources and local dependencies within the workspace are versioned according to the history rules. Build folders, caches and Git metadata are excluded. Binary files can be saved, but their differences are not shown as text. Snapshot limits are 4,000 files, 128 MiB total and 32 MiB per file; exceeding them needs a smaller source scope, not unlimited automatic copying.

Automated reconstruction repairs also record Git backups. A modified managed copy can show its source commit when an appropriate snapshot existed before patch creation. A source snapshot does not back up every installed engine, original game asset or external runtime.

Backup and recovery#

Preserve the project's data/history directory together with its sources when moving or backing up an installation. Do not delete a project to clear a build cache: that may remove its private history and recorded evidence. See storage for directory roles and reconstruction for source-repair workflows.

pages.title: Installation and first launch
pages.description: Keep a complete installation and check the runtime and task prerequisites.
pages.html:
Keep the complete installation together#

On Windows, start CyDecompilator.exe. On Linux, use CyDecompilator.sh with a Python runtime created for Linux. The desktop uses one private Python environment and optional, separately installed engines. A source ZIP or application update is not a complete runtime bundle. Keep the existing runtime/ and data/ directories when applying an application update.

Folder Role
app/ Application code, translations, bundled manual and notices
runtime/python/ Private interpreter and installed Python dependencies
runtime/engines/ Optional analysis engines and toolchains
data/ Projects, settings, history, jobs and reports

Do not move an existing Python virtual environment and assume it will still work: its launcher paths can be absolute. For a new development installation, create it in its final directory, then install the application requirements and the owner's CyToolsCore SDK. The developer setup is recorded in app/README.md. Linux execution and individual engines have platform-specific validation limits; Windows results do not establish Linux compatibility.

Check prerequisites by task#

  1. Open Engines. Install only what your target format requires, or select an existing compatible tool.
  2. For native source builds, install a matching C/C++ toolchain. Windows PE projects generally use the Visual Studio C++ workload and Windows SDK.
  3. For managed projects, provide a compatible .NET SDK and the target framework's references. Java analysis/builds need the appropriate Java installation. JavaScript/Electron workflows need Node.js and the selected optional components.
  4. Git is required for project history and automated source-repair backups.
  5. Configure an AI provider only if you want AI assistance. Manual decompilation does not require an AI provider.

Confirm the installation#

Open Options, select a language and theme, then press F1. The manual must open even without a project. Open a small known input before analyzing a large application. An installed engine and a successful analysis are separate states: check the job result if a component is present but produces no functions.

When launch fails#

An error about runtime/python/Scripts/pythonw.exe means the Windows launcher cannot find its private interpreter. Restore or recreate that environment at the installation location. If a native library or Python import fails, check Application log and the matching runtime requirements rather than installing packages into an unrelated system Python. See troubleshooting and storage before removing anything.

pages.title: Connect a feature to code and evidence
pages.description: Connect a visible feature to source locations, calls and observed evidence.
pages.html:
Open Investigation to connect a visible feature with candidate files, functions, resources, routes or calls. A static match is a candidate; an execution observation is separate evidence. The dossier records target hashes and source line/address locations so conclusions can be reviewed.

JavaScript, Electron and web#

  1. Select an application folder, ASAR archive, JS/TS/JSX/TSX file or HTML entry.
  2. Install the TypeScript parser if requested and provide Node.js. Start application analysis; this parser does not execute the inspected modules.
  3. Search for a visible string, HTML identifier, route, symbol, preload bridge or IPC channel.
  4. Inspect related main/preload/renderer modules and local source-map evidence. Compare mappings with the actual file/line and content identity.
  5. Import supported HAR observations or configure a runtime scenario to strengthen the investigation.

Source maps can be incomplete, stale or absent. An IPC channel name does not prove which handler ran. Indirect calls, dynamic route registration and computed module paths can remain unresolved. External services, credentials and unavailable backend code cannot be recovered from a frontend bundle alone.

Native investigation#

Select an analyzed native project and the function of interest. Supported Ghidra-backed dossiers expose types, instructions and high-pcode/value-use evidence. Match instruction locations to the intended module and preserve address-base information. A matching numeric address in another module is insufficient attribution. See native analysis for exports, strings and calling conventions.

  1. Choose versions — Record identities and prerequisites.

pages.title: .NET, Java, Python and shaders
pages.description: Understand the supported .NET, Java, Android, Python and shader workflows.
pages.html:
Managed .NET#

Use ILSpy to inspect C# and recover a source project with available references/resources. A .NET SDK is needed to build; targeting packs and original dependencies may also be necessary. Recovered names and control flow can differ from original source, especially after obfuscation. A .NET single-file host may need extraction before selecting the managed assembly.

For source editing, diagnostics, completion and formatting, attach the recovered project in Project IDE. Source-method replacement and debugging have their own requirements; see patching and debugging. Generated state-machine/helper methods should be edited through their owning source method rather than selected as independent replacement targets.

Java and Android#

Vineflower handles Java classes/JARs; JADX handles Android DEX/APK and supported Java inputs. Install their required Java runtime in Engines. Check decompiler warnings and resource output. Recovered Java is useful for understanding, but a complete Android build may still need the original Gradle setup, SDK, signing configuration, assets and dependencies. There is no general one-click Android rebuild guarantee.

Python bytecode#

The Python engine uses format-aware bytecode tools. Source recovery covers supported bytecode versions through Python 3.8; newer versions can still have bytecode views without original-source reconstruction. The application runtime's Python version does not change the version of the input bytecode. PyInstaller extraction can expose bundled files, which can then be opened individually. Missing modules, native extensions and runtime resources still need reconstruction separately.

GPU shaders#

The built-in shader engine handles supported DXBC SM4/5, DXIL SM6 and SPIR-V inputs. It produces HLSL/GLSL or instruction/bytecode views according to the format and available information. Compare register/resource bindings, entry points and control flow with the original shader evidence.

Compilation checks require the appropriate verifier/compiler and are reported separately from decompilation. A successful shader compile does not prove identical images, pipeline state, resource layouts or GPU performance. Use observed behavior and the real rendering scenario when validating graphics changes. A shader decompiler is not a complete graphics-engine source converter.

pages.title: Native code and executable details
pages.description: Inspect PE/ELF code, references, symbols and recoverable C functions.
pages.html:
What native analysis recovers#

The built-in C engine covers supported x86, x64 and ARM64 paths in PE/ELF files. It can recover structured control flow, arithmetic, selected floating-point/SIMD operations and inferred call prototypes. The native disassembler exposes instructions even when a function cannot be reconstructed as C. Ghidra provides an optional deeper investigation path with types, instructions and high-pcode evidence.

Treat inferred types, function boundaries, calling conventions and indirect-call targets as working interpretations. Unsupported instructions or incomplete control flow are reasons to inspect disassembly and the report, not to assume the pseudocode is complete.

Inspect one feature#

  1. Open the executable and confirm its architecture, load layout and entry points.
  2. Find a related string, import, export or known symbol in Workspace.
  3. Follow callers/callees and compare recovered C with the corresponding instructions.
  4. Use Investigation for an instruction/type/value dossier when the Ghidra path is available.
  5. Record the function/address, input identity, evidence and remaining unknowns before changing code.

Export C and reconstruct#

The Program controls can export selected native functions, exported functions, or a function and its callees as supported. Recovered globals, constants and imports are included where available. Project IDE can prepare executable, DLL or static-library targets with CMake and Windows Visual Studio project files. Missing entry points, imports, data exports, TLS initialization or resources can still block a runnable reconstruction.

Generated C that compiles is not automatically behaviorally equivalent. Check pointer widths, structure layouts, ownership, callback conventions and initialization. A leaf-function patch has stricter constraints than a full reconstructed project; see replacement plans.

Containers, packing and symbols#

Available executable details include section entropy, overlay, embedded resources, protections, manifests and toolchain indicators. Extraction supports recognized PyInstaller, .NET single-file, UPX and appended ZIP cases. Extracted material needs its own analysis; detection does not imply successful unpacking or decryption.

Symbols can improve names, but do not recover every original type or source file. Sectionless ELF input may use validated load segments; missing symbol/relocation information still limits results. Console module identities and indirect native value dependencies may remain unresolved. Keep these gaps in the final investigation report.

pages.title: Compare output, network and graphical behavior
pages.description: Record and compare output, file changes, network activity and graphical scenarios.
pages.html:
In Investigation → Version behavior, configure two versions and the same repeatable scenario. Set launch arguments, stdin, initial files, deadlines and the observation driver. Start only the application you intend to test; recorded behavior comes from launched processes and supported child processes.

  1. Choose versions — Record identities and prerequisites.
  2. Define actions — Use the same inputs and checks.
  3. Run separately — Bound time and process ownership.
  4. Capture evidence — Outputs, files, screens, network.
  5. Compare — Inspect differences and missing data.
  6. Scope the claim — Only observed checks are established.

Choose a driver#

Driver Requirements and scope
Windows controls Accessible UI Automation controls; private .NET Framework recorder
Chromium Compatible Chrome/Edge executable, scenario URL and Node.js 22+
Electron renderer Application executable, Node.js 22+ and, if ambiguous, the exact renderer URL

Build steps with the graphical scenario editor, or use advanced JSON. CSS selectors must identify one element in web drivers. For example, adapt these selectors and expected text to your own application:

json
[  {"action":"fill","selector":"#name","text":"Report"},  {"action":"click","selector":"#go"},  {"action":"assertText","selector":"#result","text":"Done","timeoutMs":5000},  {"action":"snapshot"}]

Windows selectors use objects such as an automationId instead of CSS. Available actions depend on the driver; password filling is refused. The scenario editor offers action, selector, text and delay fields, plus add/update/remove controls.

Read the evidence#

Observed differences compares enabled outputs, files, control states, HTTP/TCP observations and console messages. Captured screens loads hash-verified images for both versions at the chosen step. Network recordings displays request method/URL/status/MIME/size, initiator stacks where available and sampled process TCP connections. Observation near a step is temporal association, not proof that the step caused a request.

HTTP capture omits headers, cookies, bodies and WebSocket frames. TCP sampling can miss short connections and does not record UDP or packet contents. Electron activity before renderer attachment can be absent. PNG comparison is exact: animation, cursor and theme changes may differ without a functional regression.

Bounds and conclusions#

Limits include 30 steps, 10 seconds per wait, 2,000 HTTP requests, 5,000 TCP observations, 500 console messages, 1,000 state elements and 8 native windows. PNG storage is bounded to 16 MiB per image and 128 MiB per scenario. Missing captures, failed steps, unfinished requests or reached limits make evidence incomplete. A matching report concerns its enabled criteria and recorded scenario only. Use reconstruction to apply these comparisons to rebuilt outputs.

pages.title: behavior_capture
pages.description: Run an explicitly selected executable in a fresh working directory. Record text streams, exit status, file changes, optional owned TCP connections and Windows/Chromium/Electron graphical scenarios. This is not an OS sandbox; external file writes and traffic outside the observation scope are not captured.
pages.html:
Run an explicitly selected executable in a fresh working directory. Record text streams, exit status, file changes, optional owned TCP connections and Windows/Chromium/Electron graphical scenarios. This is not an OS sandbox; external file writes and traffic outside the observation scope are not captured.

Signature#

text
op_behavior_capture(parameters: {projectId, executable, arguments, stdin, assetsDirectory, seedFiles, timeout, observation}) -> jobId

Submit a Runtime job, wait for its terminal state and inspect its outputs or error. MCP and CLI usage.

Parameters#

Name Type Required Description
projectId string Yes Project id returned by open_file or list_projects.
executable string Yes Absolute executable path.
arguments array No Command arguments, including an absolute script path for Node.js.
stdin string No Finite text input.
assetsDirectory string No Optional folder copied into the working directory.
seedFiles object No Relative filename to UTF-8 text; same setup for both versions.
timeout integer No Maximum capture seconds.
observation object No Optional replay and network recording.
observation.driver string No Graphical driver.
observation.network boolean No Sample owned TCP connections and record selected renderer HTTP metadata.
observation.url string No Navigate the owned renderer to this URL.
observation.targetUrl string No Exact renderer URL when multiple pages exist.
observation.headless boolean No Chromium only: render without a visible browser window.
observation.steps array No Up to 30 click/fill/wait/assertText/snapshot steps; CSS selectors for web, selector object with automationId/name/controlType for Windows. Windows also toggle/select; web also press/navigate.
observation.settleMs integer No Wait after each step before recording state.
observation.stopAfterScenario boolean No Stop the owned target after the scenario, including a failed step.

Returns#

Name Type Required Description
captureId string No Persistent recording id.
changes array No Created, modified and deleted files.
complete boolean No Process observation completed within limits.

pages.title: managed_patch_prepare
pages.description: Build the edited C# project and replace a selected source method in a verified preview of the original assembly. Import isolated compiler-generated closures/local functions and async/iterator state machines. Remap IL and verify all existing other method bodies/tokens unchanged. Optionally import compatible new user-defined dependencies and emit remapped portable PDBs. Reject signature/layout/initializer changes, R2R and mixed mode.
pages.html:
Build the edited C# project and replace a selected source method in a verified preview of the original assembly. Import isolated compiler-generated closures/local functions and async/iterator state machines. Remap IL and verify all existing other method bodies/tokens unchanged. Optionally import compatible new user-defined dependencies and emit remapped portable PDBs. Reject signature/layout/initializer changes, R2R and mixed mode.

Signature#

text
op_managed_patch_prepare(parameters: {projectId, methodId, donor, configuration, targetProject, build, removeStrongName, allowNewMembers, symbols}) -> jobId

Submit a Runtime job, wait for its terminal state and inspect its outputs or error. MCP and CLI usage.

Parameters#

Name Type Required Description
projectId string Yes Project id returned by open_file or list_projects.
methodId string Yes Metadata token returned by managed_methods, e.g. 0x06000001.
donor string No Rebuilt assembly path relative to source workspace; empty = unique matching bin output.
configuration string No Configuration.
targetProject string No Optional startup/source .csproj relative to the solution folder.
build boolean No Build the attached source project before preparing.
removeStrongName boolean No Explicitly allow removing an existing strong-name signature; may break dependent assemblies.
allowNewMembers boolean No Import new reachable user-defined methods/types and compatible fields; existing constructors/layouts remain protected.
symbols boolean No Build portable symbols and remap selected/imported method sequence points into the patched assembly.

Returns#

planId string No Verified patch plan.

generatedTypes array No Isolated generated types added by this replacement.

addedTypes array No All added types.
addedMethods array No All added methods.
addedFields array No All added fields.
symbols boolean No Regenerated portable PDB available.
unchangedMethods integer No Other methods verified unchanged.

filesystemExternal, processSpawn, network

pages.title: open_file
pages.description: Open a binary, assembly, archive, bytecode or shader file as a project (deduplicated by SHA256), detect its format and, by default, analyze it with the best installed engine.
pages.html:
Open a binary, assembly, archive, bytecode or shader file as a project (deduplicated by SHA256), detect its format and, by default, analyze it with the best installed engine.

Signature#

text
op_open_file(parameters: {path, analyze, engine, force, options}) -> jobId

Submit a Runtime job, wait for its terminal state and inspect its outputs or error. MCP and CLI usage.

Parameters#

Name Type Required Description
path string Yes Absolute path of the file to open.
analyze boolean No Run the analysis immediately.
engine string No Engine id. Empty selects the analysed (or best available) engine for the file.
force boolean No Re-analyze even if an analysis already exists.
options object No Engine options.
options.maxDecompile integer No Ghidra: functions decompiled during analysis; others on demand.
options.functionTimeout integer No Ghidra: decompiler timeout per function, seconds.
options.analysisTimeout integer No Ghidra: auto-analysis timeout, seconds.
options.processor string No Ghidra: language id for raw binaries, e.g. ARM:LE:32:v8 or x86:LE:64:default.
options.decodeResources boolean No JADX: decode AndroidManifest.xml and resources.
options.deobfuscate boolean No JADX: rename obfuscated short names.
options.javaHeapMb integer No JADX: Java heap in MiB.
options.symbols boolean No PE files: load PDB debug symbols (local folders, then the configured symbol server) and apply their names (native engine and Ghidra).

Returns#

Name Type Required Description
projectId string No Project id.
format object No Detected format.
analyses object No Analyses by engine.
engine string No Engine used.

Replace sample paths and IDs with values from your installation and previous job outputs. Save this object in a parameters file or use it inside the MCP parameters envelope.

Preserve the original signature/ABI.

Compile a native x86/x64 PE replacement. Default mode verifies a leaf function in place; extended mode appends linked code/data, resolves existing functions/imports, merges x64 unwind tables and ASLR relocations, and redirects the original entry. Preserve the original signature/ABI.

nativeTarget string No New native target.
entryFunction string No Optional native application entry function.
maxRounds integer No Maximum build rounds.
repair boolean No Apply bounded AI source repairs saved to Git.
runTests boolean No Run the recovered project tests.
verifyBehavior boolean No Capture and compare behavior after a successful build.
configuration string No Build configuration.
targetProject string No Startup project relative to workspace for multi-project .NET solutions.
scenarios array No Up to ten scenarios: name, arguments, stdin, timeout, seedFiles, assetsDirectory, observation (same behavior_capture contract), runtimeExecutable (absolute Electron/Chromium runtime), optional originalExecutable/originalArguments, rebuiltExecutable (relative to workspace)/rebuiltArguments, checks {stdout,stderr,exitCode,files,network,graphics} (default all true), normalizeApplicationPaths (default true for Electron file URLs). Empty chooses an inferred scenario if runnable.

status string No scenarios-matched, compiled-unverified, compilation-failed, tests-failed, behavior-differs, blocked or cancelled.
attempts array No Build results, repair evidence, comparisons and Git commits.
unknowns array No Unverified behavior and missing evidence.

pages.title: Replace a function in an application copy
pages.description: Prepare a native or .NET function replacement and write a separate application copy.
pages.html:
The Function patch page produces a modified copy after compiling and checking a replacement. It does not edit arbitrary functions in place while an application is running. Keep the original, source version and patch receipt together so a result remains traceable.

  1. Select target — Confirm method and input identity.
  2. Edit source — Preserve the external contract.
  3. Compile a plan — Check code and required bindings.
  4. Review warnings — Inspect size, IL or relocations.
  5. Create a copy — Retain original and receipt.
  6. Validate behavior — Test the requested change.

Native x86/x64 Windows PE#

  1. Select the function in Workspace, then open Project IDE → Function patch → Edit selected function.
  2. Preserve its signature, calling convention, pointer sizes and observable contract. Start with an autonomous supported C function.
  3. Choose the replacement symbol and use Compile and verify patch. Review compiled instructions, byte capacity, warnings and bindings.
  4. For supported larger functions, the extended linking option can append a native section and redirect the original entry. Calls, data, relocations and unwind information need valid bindings; this is not an unrestricted native linker.
  5. Choose Write modified copy only for a current valid plan. Then analyze/run the saved copy and compare the intended behavior.

Unsupported architectures/formats, entry sizes, unresolved symbols and unsafe relocations can block a plan. C pseudocode that compiles in isolation is not sufficient proof of a compatible replacement.

Managed .NET method#

  1. Create/attach the C# source project and choose Load .NET methods.
  2. Select an editable source method, then Edit declaring type. Change its source and save.
  3. Use Build and verify method patch. The donor assembly must correspond to the selected project/method.
  4. Review IL changes, generated dependencies and verification of other methods before writing the modified copy.
  5. Run or debug the saved copy with matching symbols and a defined scenario.

Supported compiler-generated dependencies can be imported with the owning method; they are not separate free-form targets. Strong-name removal is an explicit option and can break dependencies. Signing requirements are not automatically repaired.

After creation#

Saved modified copies retains receipts and source commits where available. Analyze modified copy reopens it for inspection. Run modified copy needs valid arguments and a timeout; a library needs a test harness. New source edits require saving and preparing a fresh plan. Do not reuse a receipt after changing its binary or dependencies. See debugging, history and validation.

pages.title: Editable source projects
pages.description: Create or attach a source project, edit files and run build commands.
pages.html:
Open Project IDE after selecting an analysis project. Create source project creates a supported editable workspace; opening/attaching an existing source folder is a separate action. An attached folder remains persistent user source: it must not be treated as a temporary job directory.

Supported reconstruction targets#

Family Produced project Remaining requirements
.NET ILSpy C#, resources, solution/project files SDK, references, startup project and target framework
Native Windows PE C, CMake, VC++ solution/project; EXE, DLL or static target C++ toolchain, recovered entry/imports/resources
Native ELF C sources and CMake target Compatible host/toolchain, ABI and missing initialization
Node/TS/web Recovered sources/resources and build configuration Node.js, required dependencies and entry points
Electron main/preload/renderer sources, ASAR-capable output Matching Electron runtime and native-module ABI

These targets are reconstruction paths, not a promise to recreate every application. Check reported blockers before assuming the output can run.

Edit and build#

  1. Create or attach the workspace and inspect the solution/file tree.
  2. Select a file to open it. Source editing supports the retained native editor, undo/redo and the services available for its language.
  3. Save changes before building. Choose the intended configuration and startup target for multi-project solutions.
  4. Use Build/Rebuild/Clean as available. Review both Build output and Problems. Click a navigable diagnostic to open its source location.
  5. Run or debug a newly validated output; stale or changed artifacts may require a new build.

Source services and limits#

The C# assistance panel provides diagnostics and supported symbol operations using local SDK services. Completions and refactoring previews depend on references and project state. Review a rename/format preview before applying it. External edits and stale source revisions can cause an operation to be refused instead of overwriting newer text.

Use Git history before broad edits and reconstruct and validate for bounded automatic build/repair attempts. The project editor is an integrated reconstruction environment; it does not implement every Rider/Visual Studio feature or supply missing proprietary SDKs.

pages.title: PS5 input preparation and desktop conversion
pages.description: Prepare readable inputs, configure AnyPS5/UltraPack and test converted output.
pages.html:
Open PS5 porting. CyDecompilator handles preserved inputs, analysis, conversion jobs, receipts and test scenarios. Optional AnyPS5 supplies executable conversion and console API/GPU compatibility; UltraPack supplies supported container extraction. These are separate backends, not an original graphics engine automatically rewritten as native PC source.

  1. Preserve resources — Inspect complete, readable input.
  2. Select backend — Install the optional compatible tool.
  3. Convert or generate — Review unsupported code and imports.
  4. Record identities — Keep the output receipt and logs.
  5. Asserted run — Test intended behavior explicitly.
  6. Assess compatibility — Build success is not full gameplay.

Prepare and convert#

  1. Under Porting tools, install/configure the converter and libraries for the intended desktop OS. Configure UltraPack for supported PKG/PFS/archive inputs; building its package helper requires .NET SDK 9+.
  2. Select an application file or a complete extracted folder containing its entry, modules and resources. Choose a relative entry if multiple applications are present.
  3. Use Prepare input, inspect metadata and missing prerequisites, then Convert for desktop. The original stays separate. Opaque/encrypted essential executable bytes are not made available merely by importing a container.
  4. Review converter diagnostics. Automatic failure analysis can connect a converter attempt to bounded C/disassembly evidence and unresolved imports. A diagnosis failure is separate from conversion failure.
  5. Configure asserted scenarios and run the verified output. Inspect receipts and failures before reusing a conversion.

Standalone homebrew is an explicit mode with stricter module assumptions. Secondary root executables differ from shared PRX modules and need a capable converter. Converting the entry alone does not establish a complete application.

Test evidence and performance#

Conversion starts as converted-unverified. Execution without assertions remains executed-unverified. Define expected stdout/exit values or other supported checks from independent intended behavior; do not copy the new output merely to make a test pass. A passing assertion covers that scenario only.

Experimental native graphics profiles replace specific compatibility paths and have their own identity/driver constraints. They do not prove complete graphics reconstruction, full gameplay or 60 FPS. Measure the same representative scene only after a meaningful change, with a bounded deadline and preserved evidence. Keep conversion disk use under review: storage explains originals, generated outputs and caches. Use AI Port and test for the same operations through an agent.

pages.title: Reconstruct, compile and validate
pages.description: Run bounded builds, optional repairs and representative behavior comparisons.
pages.html:
In Project IDE → Reconstruction, Reconstruct and validate chains workspace creation, builds, optional source repair and recorded behavior comparisons. Define the intended behavior before enabling automatic attempts. A missing entry point, unsupported dependency or unavailable original cannot be solved by increasing the retry count alone.

  1. Original behavior — Define a repeatable scenario.
  2. Editable project — Recover sources and resources.
  3. Resolve blockers — Check ABI, entries and dependencies.
  4. Build and repair — Bound attempts; back up sources.
  5. Replay tests — Run the intended assertions.
  6. Review result — Separate builds from matching behavior.

Prepare the run#

  1. Open/analyze the input and review the project target.
  2. Configure the compiler/runtime, references and startup target. Save all open files.
  3. Configure test scenarios with expected behavior and the original/reconstructed launch commands. Use investigation scenario imports the current observation configuration.
  4. Choose a bounded number of build attempts. Automatic AI repairs require a configured provider and Git; the first build counts toward the limit.
  5. Start reconstruction. Sources are protected from concurrent editing while the workflow updates them. Cancel through the task controls if necessary.

Repairs are source changes with revision checks and Git backups. An outdated response or an external source modification interrupts application of the repair. AI text is not treated as an arbitrary terminal command.

Interpret the final state#

Result Meaning
Build failed / reconstruction blocked Read diagnostics and unresolved prerequisites
Built; behavior unverified A fresh build exists; sufficient execution evidence does not
Project tests failed The project's requested tests failed
Behavior differs At least one enabled comparison criterion differs
Recorded scenarios match Enabled assertions agree for the recorded scenarios only

Use Inspect recorded comparison to examine saved evidence in Investigation. Reports retain attempts, changes, source commits, diagnostics and capture identities. Libraries need an appropriate test executable. A GUI scenario must cover the interaction of interest; a launch-only check cannot validate a feature.

Web and Electron projects#

The workspace configuration records kind, entry, build script and output directory. A configured npm build/test script runs when requested; locked dependency installation uses its separate explicit action. Native modules still require a matching runtime/ABI. A generated ASAR is not a signed installer. Rebuild after source or artifact changes. Missing servers, remote APIs, credentials and external resources are not reconstructed automatically.

Continue with observed behavior, AI workflows and troubleshooting.

pages.title: Preferences, updates and licenses
pages.description: Adjust appearance, languages, providers, application updates and license notices.
pages.html:
Open Options to change interface settings. Language, theme, density and text size are local application preferences. Changing them does not modify analysis results or project source files.

Language and appearance#

The interface starts in English and offers English, French, German, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, Russian, Simplified Chinese, Japanese and Korean. Select a language to apply it without restarting. The bundled manual is fully available in English and French; its language selector can override the interface choice. Other interface languages fall back to the English manual.

Themes include Mid grey, Light grey, Amber night, Violet and Navy. Density and text scaling alter layout; narrower windows move some panels into tabs. Resetting interface preferences does not remove models, source files, provider settings or analysis data. In the documentation's enlarged-image view, use wheel zoom, drag to pan and double-click fit.

Configuration and updates#

Generation configurations save supported operation parameters, not private credential secrets. Review the chosen configuration before applying it to a different project. Installation storage settings distinguish the local installation from optional shared caches.

Application updates, engine updates and AI-provider/model settings are separate. Application updating stages and verifies an archive, checks runtime compatibility and retains rollback material. Keep data/ and runtime/ when updating application code. A release ZIP may require an existing compatible private runtime; inspect its release notes. Do not overwrite an installation with a mismatched Python/runtime bundle.

License notices#

The Options license section lists the application and declared engines/dependencies with their original notices where available. CyUI's MIT notice is bundled locally even when its source repository is private. A link requiring repository access does not prevent reading the included notice. Translated interface labels are not translations of the legal texts, and a dependency's license does not replace the application's own license.

For missing libraries, incompatible updates or settings issues, see installation, storage and troubleshooting.

pages.title: Welcome to CyDecompilator
pages.description: Choose a workflow, inspect a first input and navigate this manual.
pages.html:
CyDecompilator inspects compiled applications, recovers code, and helps create, edit and test supported source projects. This manual is included with the application: reading it needs no internet, installed analysis engine, AI account or open project.

Find your way#

Press F1 from any page to open its guide. Select Documentation in the sidebar or the Ctrl+Shift+P command palette to open the installed CyDoc reader in your browser using a local file URL. Use the global search field at the top or Ctrl+K to search the complete text, the section list to jump within a chapter, and the browser’s Back / Forward controls to revisit pages. Use the image enlargement control to expand it inside the reader window; scroll to zoom, drag to pan and double-click to reset. Escape reduces an enlarged view. Code blocks have a Copy button. Documentation links open another chapter; external website links open separately and are unnecessary for reading the local manual.

English is the default. The manual follows an English/French interface preference until you select its own language. Other interface languages use the English manual. Both translations contain the same chapters, illustrations and workflows.

First useful result#

  1. Read installation and open Engines to check the tool you need.
  2. Open Workspace. Choose a supported file with Ctrl+O, or paste its path and press Enter.
  3. Select an engine, wait for analysis, then select a function. Inspect the recovered source and disassembly together.
  4. Use Project IDE for editable sources, Investigation for evidence, or AI for an assisted workflow.
  5. Save useful notes and source changes. Keep the original input and review the recorded errors and unknowns.
  1. Preserve input — Keep original bytes separate.
  2. Inspect format — Confirm architecture and contents.
  3. Choose an engine — Check its prerequisites.
  4. Analyze — Read progress and diagnostics.
  5. Inspect code — Compare functions and instructions.
  6. Record findings — Keep evidence and unknowns.

Choose a goal#

Goal Guide
Understand a function or recover names Workspace and native analysis
Rebuild an editable application Projects and reconstruct and validate
Change one function in an application copy Function replacement
Investigate an Electron feature JavaScript and native investigation
Compare two versions, network and UI behavior Observed behavior
Drive work through an AI client AI and MCP / CLI
Prepare console input or consult Unreal rules PS5, Xbox, Unreal

Read results accurately#

Recovered code is not the original source project. Compilation establishes that a toolchain accepted the generated project; it does not establish the original behavior. Matching scenarios cover only their recorded interactions and assertions. Unsupported instructions, missing dependencies, unavailable resources and untested platforms remain explicit limitations. A page absent from your installed version is unavailable in that version; updating application code does not install its optional engines.

pages.title: Storage, backups and original files
pages.description: Distinguish originals, generated projects, caches and recoverable backups.
pages.html:
Large applications and console inputs can consume far more disk space than the CyDecompilator code. Inspect free space before extraction, conversion or repeated test copies. Cancelling a job does not imply that every persistent output or partial download has been removed.

Understand directory ownership#

Location Contents Preservation
Original input location Your application, resources or archive Keep as the independent original
data/projects/ Imported snapshots, analysis, editable sources, history and receipts Persistent project data; back up intentionally
data/settings/ Interface and application settings Preserve during updates
data/jobs/ and reports Task state, outputs and evidence Check references before removing old work
runtime/python/ Private interpreter/dependencies Needed to launch; not a disposable build cache
runtime/engines/ Installed optional tools Separate from one project's build
runtime/build/, downloads, staging/backups Generated work, downloads, update material Review exact subdirectory and active use
dist/ Prepared distribution archives Separate from running projects
  1. Original input — Keep the independent original.
  2. Analysis project — Store identity and recovered evidence.
  3. Editable sources — Know which folder owns the files.
  4. Git snapshot — Back up meaningful source changes.
  5. Tested output — Keep the useful artifact and receipt.
  6. Review cleanup — Remove only identified unused work.

Avoid unnecessary duplication#

Use existing compatible engines rather than copying a full toolchain for each test. Registering an existing native project can keep a dependency on its current location; know which folder owns its resources. A whole application folder, extracted archive, conversion output and fresh test copy can each occupy significant space. Source-history limits do not bound all of these copies.

Clean deliberately#

Stop related jobs and inspect the exact directory before removing generated build output, obsolete test captures or old downloads. Preserve the latest useful output, reports required for validation, source-history repositories, original inputs and active runtime components. Deleting a project's data can also delete editable sources and history; it is not equivalent to cleaning compiler objects.

Back up sources, persistent project data and necessary external dependencies together. A Git source snapshot is useful but does not contain every game asset, installed runtime or provider configuration. No documentation button automatically deletes files or starts cleanup.

Registering an existing native project can keep a dependency on its current location; know which folder owns its resources. pages.title: Troubleshooting and result states
pages.description: Locate failures, interpret result states and recover without losing source work.
pages.html:
Open Application log and the relevant task output. Record the operation, selected input/project, engine, source revision, final state and error. Read the first actionable error as well as the final summary; later compiler messages can be consequences of an earlier missing dependency.

Locate the failure#

Symptom Next check
Application does not start Private interpreter, matching native dependencies and launcher log
Engine missing Engines page, executable path and required Java/.NET/Node version
No functions / partial code Detected format, architecture, packing and unsupported instructions
Build fails Compiler, references, entry point, resources and current diagnostics
Build succeeds but Run is refused Fresh artifact identity, startup target and required runtime
Patch preparation fails Signature/ABI, capacity, relocations, donor method and source revision
Debugger has no variables Active pause/frame, symbols and optimization
AI request fails Selected provider/model, existing login/key, limits and provider output
Scenario incomplete Driver, selectors, deadlines, unsupported actions and capture limits
Menu absent Installed application/module version and applicable workflow
Disk fills up Imported/extracted resources, repeated outputs, snapshots and test copies

Interpret states instead of only colors#

Queued, Preparing and Running are intermediate job states. Completed, Failed and Cancelled are terminal Runtime states. Completed means the handler returned: inspect its business result, which may still report a failed build, differences or unverified execution. A cancelled job can retain useful partial diagnostics without a successful result.

For reconstruction, distinguish build success from project tests and recorded scenario agreement. For console conversion, distinguish prepared, converted-unverified, executed-unverified and asserted scenario success. For patches, a valid plan precedes creation of a verified modified-copy receipt. Never promote an old successful run after its input/output hashes changed.

Recover without losing work#

Save editor buffers, stop related processes and inspect the latest source-history checkpoint. Rebuild or regenerate a plan after relevant changes. Fix missing tools before retrying; do not repeatedly run the same long scenario when no meaningful change occurred. Before clearing files, consult storage. Use a small representative example to separate a general installation problem from one unsupported application.

pages.title: Unreal reconstruction knowledge
pages.description: Consult reconstruction rules and campaign profiles before implementing a subsystem.
pages.html:
Open Unreal reconstruction to consult the bundled methodology and campaign-profile catalogue. This page provides reconstruction knowledge and source identities. It does not automatically convert a console game into a working Unreal project or embed the Unreal Editor inside CyDecompilator.

Use the catalogue#

  1. Select the general methodology or an available specific profile.
  2. Filter rules by category and inspect prerequisites, evidence and unresolved behavior.
  3. Copy the displayed reconstruction guide when needed; it includes relevant source identities/hashes.
  4. Use the corresponding Runtime/MCP rule and guide operations for an agent-driven investigation.

The catalogue covers reconstruction concerns such as geometry/UVs, materials, animation, navigation, weapons, AI, vehicles, effects and audio. Specific profiles retain their own executable identity and model assumptions. A game title alone is insufficient to establish that a profile applies to your files.

From knowledge to a validated subsystem#

Define one observable feature, identify its input resources and functions, record the relevant original behavior, then implement and test the proposed replacement in an appropriate source project. Compare representative rendering, controls, timing and outputs. Keep unsupported behavior explicit instead of treating rules as implementation proof.

  1. Original behavior — Define a repeatable scenario.
  2. Editable project — Recover sources and resources.
  3. Resolve blockers — Check ABI, entries and dependencies.
  4. Build and repair — Bound attempts; back up sources.
  5. Replay tests — Run the intended assertions.
  6. Review result — Separate builds from matching behavior.

What remains separate#

Asset import, project generation, code implementation, an Unreal installation and actual builds/execution remain separate work. The rules catalogue can be read without game files; an actual conversion needs the appropriate sources/resources and development environment. No generic PS3/PS4/PS5/Xbox-to-Unreal conversion or performance guarantee follows from rule consultation.

Use native analysis and Investigation to find evidence, Projects for source work, and observations to compare testable behavior. The catalogue's original reference snapshots are distinct from the reconstructed output's own version history.
